text: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke met West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, reaffirming support for the INDIA bloc rally while saying the party will not join it. Banerjee praised the CJP’s youth movement and invited its activists to organise programmes in Bengal, Times of India, Outlook India and The Tribune report.

sources.title: 'Cockroach Janta Party Is An Independent Organisation,' Dipke Says CJP Backs INDIA Bloc Protest But Won't Participate - Outlook India
sources.articleText:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the party supported the campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and would stand by any organisation raising concerns over alleged vote theft
The Cockroach Janta Party has backed the INDIA bloc’s protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar but ruled out formally participating.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the party would support any organisation campaigning against alleged electoral manipulation.
Mamata Banerjee acknowledged the CJP’s support as Opposition parties prepare the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has expressed solidarity with the INDIA bloc’s protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar but ruled out formally participating in the rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, saying it wants to maintain its independent identity.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the party supported the campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and would stand by any organisation raising concerns over alleged vote theft. However, he clarified that the outfit would not join the Opposition-led mobilisation.
“We support the protest tomorrow, we stand in solidarity, but the Cockroach Janta Party is an independent organisation; it is a neutral platform, and we want to keep it that way,” Dipke said after meeting former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Saturday.
Emphasising that the issue extended beyond individual political organisations, Dipke said the CJP would support any group campaigning against alleged electoral manipulation.
“Anybody who will fight against this vote theft, we will support all organisations,” he said.

The CJP had earlier announced its backing for the INDIA bloc’s rally , which is seeking Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
In a statement posted on X, the party accused the Chief Election Commissioner of undermining the credibility of the electoral process through the revision exercise.
“By undermining this very principle through SIR, Gyanesh Kumar has lost the trust required to oversee free and fair elections. His resignation is therefore necessary to restore the credibility and independence of the Election Commission,” the statement said.
Banerjee also acknowledged the CJP’s backing for the Opposition’s campaign, describing INDIA bloc leaders as pioneers of the movement.
“They have extended their full support for tomorrow’s rally, and we have extended all support to them as well. They are the pioneers and the founders of this movement. That we must remember,” Banerjee told reporters.
Opposition parties are organising the ‘Chalo Dilli’ march and the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally at Ramlila Maidan to protest against alleged electoral irregularities and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar .
The INDIA bloc has raised concerns over the SIR exercise, alleging that it could lead to the exclusion of eligible voters from electoral rolls. The Election Commission has maintained that the revision is part of the process of updating voter lists.

sources.title: Dipke meets Mamata Banerjee; says CJP wont join INDIA bloc rally but supports cause - The Tribune
sources.articleText:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday met Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee in Delhi, thanking her for supporting the outfit’s youth-led protests and expressing solidarity with the INDIA bloc’s rally against alleged electoral irregularities.
However, Dipke made it clear that CJP would maintain its independent identity and would not participate in Sunday’s Opposition rally at Ramlila Maidan.
Dipke said he had met Banerjee to thank her for standing by the organisation during its first protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak and for later supporting its activists when CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested by the Delhi Police.
“I just came to say thank you to Didi because the way she supported our first Jantar Mantar movement, she was always so strongly with the youth movement. When Saurav and Ashutosh were arrested by the Delhi Police, even then Didi stood with us very firmly,” he said.
Asked whether CJP would join Sunday’s rally, Dipke said the organisation supported the INDIA bloc’s protest but would continue to function as an independent and neutral platform.
“We support the protest tomorrow, we stand in solidarity, but the Cockroach Janta Party is an independent organisation; it is a neutral platform, and we want to keep it that way,” he said.
Emphasising that the fight against alleged vote theft extended beyond individual political parties or organisations, Dipke said CJP would support anyone taking up the issue.
“Anybody who will fight against this vote theft, we will support all organisations,” he said.
Banerjee, who is in the national capital to attend Sunday’s rally, praised Dipke and the young activists for their role in protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission.
“They have extended their full support for tomorrow’s rally, and we have extended all support to them as well. They are the pioneers and the founders of this movement. That we must remember,” she told reporters.
She also invited Dipke and other CJP activists to West Bengal to organise programmes, leaving the decision to the organisation.
The meeting came a day before the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, where Opposition parties are expected to raise allegations of electoral irregularities and demand accountability from the Election Commission.
